`interface IClockBridge`<br/>
**Extends:** [`IBridge`](/reference/bridges/ibridge/)<br/>
**Known subtypes:** [`ManualClockBridge`](/reference/bridges/manualclockbridge/), [`SystemClockBridge`](/reference/bridges/systemclockbridge/)<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.bridge.clock` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [IClockBridge.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/bridge/clock/IClockBridge.java)

The bridge that gives JOID the time read by animations, tweens, media and drags.

## Description

`BridgeHandler.CLOCK` holds a [`SystemClockBridge`](/reference/bridges/systemclockbridge/) by default; a host whose time can pause, or a test, registers its own above it.
This clock follows the time of a game, which stops while the game pauses:

```java file="com/example/backend/EngineClockBridge.java" region="clock"
```

### nanoTime

`long nanoTime()` <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span>

Returns the current time in nanoseconds, from any origin, at the same rate as `currentTimeMillis()`; JOID uses only differences of it.

<a id="IClockBridge-method-currentTimeMillis"></a>

### currentTimeMillis

`long currentTimeMillis()` <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span>

Returns the current time in milliseconds, which JOID reads as a date or as the phase of a cycle ([Clock bridge](/build/bridges/clock/#required)).
